To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the error function of the neural net is a quadratic function of the connection weights and the critical points of this function are projections of the input data onto subspaces spanned by the first few principal components of the input data.
the landscape of the error function of a neural network with respect to the weights is completely characterized by the eigenvectors of the covariance matrix of the input data.

(a) the landscape of the usual quadratic error E in a neural network is completely determined by principal components analysis, (b) E has a unique global minimum, (c) all the other critical points are saddle points, and (d) the learning algorithms converge to this minimum.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions.
the following questions: 1) Is the landscape of the error function of a layered linear feedforward neural network with quadratic error function well defined?
the following questions: 1. Is it possible to train a neural network without falling into a local minimum?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there are no local minima for the usual quadratic error criterion, but only saddle points.

the landscape associated to the error function of a layered linear feed forward network has only one minimum, which corresponds to a projection onto the subsphere generated by the first eigenvectors of the covariance matrix of the training patterns.
the learning algorithms are guaranteed to converge to the unique global minimum of E, and the saddle point critical points are never encountered.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the landscape of E in the case of linear networks with quadratic errors is a very simple one.
we show the existence and uniqueness of the global minimum in a neural network, and that this is a good thing for training.
, in the case of a layered linear feed forward network, the error function E is not a convex function.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the learning process is a process of projection onto a subspace generated by a few of the principal components of the covariance matrix of the examples, rather than a search for a minimum of a highly nonlinear error function.
the landscape of the error function is very well behaved.
the landscape of the usual quadratic error is much simpler than previously thought.
